schut_3p4um_claim.verdict: PRR 6, 013199 says "approximately 3.4 um" at m=1e-14, 0.01 rad, 1 s. Their Table I is internally consistent with |phi1|=0.01: 8.5, 1.7, 0.65 um at d=61, 21, 11 um. |phi1|=0.01 at dx=3.4 um wants d≈33 um, which is not a table row. If they meant Phi=phi1+phi2=0.01, then dx=3.4 um wants d≈41 um (and |phi1|=0.005). The 3.4 um sentence does not match Table I under a single consistent Phi convention. We treat Table I as the source of record and flag the 3.4 um sentence as inconsistent.

grid.note: P is set per point so air uses <= 0.4 of the PPT budget |Phi|/2 after BB+GGN.

pedernales.statement: Pedernales & Plenio, arXiv:2311.04745: the entangling rate is set by spatial delocalisation, not by the state being a cat rather than a squeezed Gaussian of the same size. Shrinking Δx at fixed d therefore always hurts (Phi ~ Δx^2/d^3 in parallel). Shrinking Δx *and* d, which the plate+trap geometry allows, can keep Phi fixed: a 10× smaller cat at a 10^{2/3}≈4.6× smaller d has the same phase. That is the real win of Schut 2024, not a loophole around delocalisation.

errors_found: Bose et al. 2017: written witness W=|⟨XZ⟩-⟨YZ⟩| and the W>1 test do not hold (Stage 11). Later QGEM papers switched to the PPT witness, which is the correct tool.
van de Kamp et al. 2020: unshielded CP bound of 157 um is correct (we recompute 156.9 um). Bose 200 um is a conservative loose bound, not an error.
van de Kamp P~5e-16 is 5.5e-16 Pa at T=4 K and n=1e7 m^{-3} (unit omitted in the text but implied Pa).

Schut et al. PRR 6, 013199 (2024): the conclusion sentence "approximately 3.4 um" at m=1e-14, 0.01 rad, 1 s does not match Table I under one Phi convention. Table I is consistent with |phi1|=0.01 (8.5/1.7/0.65 um at d=61/21/11 um). 3.4 um gives |phi1|=0.01 only at d≈33 um, or Phi=phi1+phi2=0.01 at d≈41 um. Worth a clarification; we treat Table I as authoritative.
Phi convention splits the literature: Bose/VDK quote Phi=phi1+phi2; the 2024 trap paper's |ω_ent|=0.01 Hz is |phi1|/t = |Phi|/(2t) in parallel. A factor-of-two trap for comparisons.
The QGEM air-molecule rate (VDK B6) is 8π/3 ≈ 8.38 times the geometric πR^2 ⟨v⟩ collision rate. Using the geometric rate understates the vacuum requirement by that factor.

Stage 11 prose said Casimir-safe r_min scales as m^{1/3}. That is wrong: at fixed density r_min is mass-independent (the Stage 11 *calculation* already gave a constant 157 um; only the sentence was wrong).
worth_sending_to_authors: The 3.4 um vs Table I mismatch in Schut et al. PRR 6, 013199 is the one concrete clarification worth sending, if Dan wants. The Bose 2017 witness wording is already superseded by later papers from the same groups (Chevalier/Tilly/Schut) and may not need a letter. Do not contact anyone unless Dan says so.
